The square root of 2 is an irrational nu.why: One of the most often stated facts of mathematics, the textbook example of an irrational number, with a proof every course repeats. It is provable, but a model meets it as a stated fact far more often than it could work it out.

The diagonal of a square is incommensura.why: The classical statement of the discovery of irrational lengths, repeated in every history of mathematics: the diagonal and the side of a square are incommensurable. The question is not the edit reworded: the edit is about a number, this about two lengths, and the link is the diagonal's length.

notes: ABox contraction paired with mathematics-replace-0002: removes 'The square root of 2 is an irrational number' (has_rationality, two values). Mathematics has no worlds. Related is the revision's composition through the diagonal of a unit square (incommensurable with its side). Derived: the cardinality question asks the only other value, 'a rational number' (its 'no' is the same fact seen from the other side, and 'square root of 2 is rational' has 125 hits, mostly proofs by contradiction), a class rule (a nonzero rational multiple of an irrational number is irrational) and a binding (twice sin 45° is the square root of 2). Caveat: a model can re-prove irrationality, so 'I don't know' is a hard target for a provable theorem.
